title: How mental exhaustion changes the choices you make

paragraphs.english: This page is an independently written reading guide to a first-person Scientific American article by researchers at Johns Hopkins University and the Kennedy Krieger Institute, first published online on 28 July 2026. Follow the original-article link below for the publisher’s full text.
paragraphs.chinese: 本页是为《科学美国人》一篇第一人称文章独立撰写的阅读导读。该文由约翰斯·霍普金斯大学与肯尼迪·克里格研究所的研究人员撰写，2026年7月28日首次在线发布。请通过下方原文链接阅读出版方提供的全文。

paragraphs.english: The article opens with a scene many parents will recognise. After a whole day of making breakfast, settling arguments, answering questions and keeping children occupied, a parent finally sits down to decide what to cook — and even that ordinary decision, with its questions about ingredients, cooking time and whether the food will be eaten at all, feels like too much.
paragraphs.chinese: 文章以一个许多父母都熟悉的场景开篇。做早饭、劝架、回答提问、陪孩子打发时间，忙了整整一天之后，家长终于坐下来想晚饭做什么——而就连这样一个普通的决定，连同其中要考虑的食材、烹饪时间以及孩子究竟会不会吃这些问题，都让人不堪重负。

paragraphs.english: The author gives this experience a name: cognitive fatigue. It is not the same as physical tiredness, and it turns up well beyond family life. An office worker who has spent the day on repetitive computer tasks may feel unable to go out with friends, and a nurse finishing a long shift may cancel an extra visit to a patient even though the visit had been planned.
paragraphs.chinese: 作者给这种体验取了一个名字：认知疲劳。它不同于身体的疲倦，而且远不只在家庭生活中出现。在电脑前做了一整天重复性工作的上班族，可能觉得自己没力气再和朋友出去；刚结束长时间值班的护士，明明原本计划好要顺路多看一位病人，也可能临到最后放弃。

paragraphs.english: To study what happens in the brain at such moments, the team scanned 28 volunteers with functional magnetic resonance imaging. Participants first worked through demanding memory exercises, then chose between two ways of earning money: an easy test that paid one dollar for a correct answer, or a harder test that could pay up to eight dollars. The cash amounts were there to give a precise price to people’s willingness to work harder.
paragraphs.chinese: 为了研究这种时刻大脑里发生了什么，团队用功能性磁共振成像扫描了28名志愿者。参与者先完成费神的记忆练习，然后在两种赚钱方式之间做选择：一种是答对一题得一美元的简单测试，另一种是答对最多可得八美元的较难测试。设置金额，是为了给人们“愿意多费力”的程度标出一个精确的价格。

paragraphs.english: The result was consistent. As participants grew more fatigued, they became much less likely to choose the demanding test, even though it offered a larger reward. Effort, in other words, was quietly becoming more expensive in their minds.
paragraphs.chinese: 结果十分一致。随着参与者越来越疲劳，他们选择困难测试的可能性明显下降，尽管那项测试的报酬更高。换句话说，在他们心里，努力正在悄悄变得更贵。

paragraphs.english: The scans pointed to a specific circuit. During the exhausting exercises, the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, an area at the front of the brain, sent increasingly strong signals to the right anterior insula, a region associated with monitoring the body’s internal state, including fatigue. The stronger the traffic between the two areas, the more likely a person was to settle for the easier option. Because the pattern could be measured, the researchers were able to use it to estimate how each volunteer traded mental effort against reward.
paragraphs.chinese: 扫描结果指向一条特定的神经回路。在那些耗时耗神的练习中，位于大脑前部的背外侧前额叶皮层向右侧前脑岛发出的信号越来越强；右侧前脑岛与监测身体内部状态（包括疲劳程度）有关。两个脑区之间的信号传递越强，人就越容易退而选择较轻松的选项。由于这一模式可以被测量，研究者得以用它来估算每位志愿者如何用脑力付出去换取报酬。

paragraphs.english: The findings matter beyond the laboratory. The article notes that severe mental exhaustion is a prominent feature of depression, long COVID and multiple sclerosis, and suggests that identifying these circuits could eventually help in designing treatments. The author is careful to say that much about severe fatigue remains unknown.
paragraphs.chinese: 这些发现的意义不止于实验室。文章指出，严重的精神疲惫是抑郁症、“长新冠”和多发性硬化症的突出表现，并认为弄清这些神经回路最终可能有助于设计治疗方案。作者也谨慎地说明，关于严重的疲劳，仍有大量问题尚不清楚。

paragraphs.english: The closing part of the article offers an evolutionary reading. Fatigue signals probably developed to stop us from overdrawing on our mental and physical reserves; when those signals are amplified, extra effort simply feels costlier. Yet the same signals can also block activities that would restore us, such as a walk outside after work, and they can stand in the way of worthwhile tasks like preparing a healthy meal. Research cited in the article suggests that understanding why an activity matters, or finding it genuinely interesting, can help people push past fatigue — in other words, reframing the task can change what we are willing to do.
paragraphs.chinese: 文章最后一部分给出了一个演化视角的解释。疲劳信号很可能是为了防止我们过度消耗心理和身体的储备而形成的；当这些信号被放大时，多付出一分努力就显得更昂贵。但同样的信号也会阻碍那些本可让我们恢复元气的活动，比如下班后到户外散步，还会妨碍诸如做一顿健康饭菜这样值得去做的事。文章引用的研究显示，理解一项活动为何重要，或从中发现真正的趣味，能帮助人越过疲劳——换句话说，重新看待手头的事，会改变我们愿意去做什么。

paragraphs.english: Here is an editor-written practice sentence, not a quotation from the original article: The more depleted the brain feels, the steeper the price it puts on effort, so a reward that once looked attractive can suddenly seem not worth the trouble.
paragraphs.chinese: 以下是编辑撰写的练习句，并非原文引句：大脑越是感到被掏空，它给努力标出的价码就越高，于是原本看来诱人的回报，可能突然显得不值得费那个劲。

paragraphs.english: As you read, watch how the article moves from everyday examples to a laboratory design and then back to ordinary life. Notice that the study does not claim people become unable to work when tired, only that their internal accounting of cost and reward shifts, and pay attention to the careful wording the author uses when discussing clinical conditions.
paragraphs.chinese: 阅读时，留意文章如何从日常场景转到实验室设计，再回到日常生活。注意这项研究并没有说人一累就无法工作，而只是说他们内心对成本与报酬的权衡发生了偏移；同时留意作者在谈到临床疾病时所用的谨慎措辞。

sentenceNotes.sentence: Because the pattern could be measured, the researchers were able to use it to estimate how each volunteer traded mental effort against reward.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: 主句为 the researchers were able to use it to estimate...，主语 the researchers，谓语 were able to use，宾语 it，to estimate 为目的不定式。
sentenceNotes.structure: 句首 Because the pattern could be measured 是原因状语从句；use it to estimate 中的 it 指代上文的信号模式；how each volunteer traded mental effort against reward 是 estimate 的宾语从句，trade A against B 表示“以A换取B”。
sentenceNotes.translation: 由于这一模式可以被测量，研究者得以用它来估算每位志愿者如何用脑力付出去换取报酬。
sentenceNotes.tip: 先看逗号后的主句，再把句首 because 从句作为原因补上。estimate 后面接的是 how 引导的宾语从句，不要把它误读成修饰 volunteer 的定语从句；trade A against B 是经济学常用搭配。

sentenceNotes.sentence: The stronger the traffic between the two areas, the more likely a person was to settle for the easier option.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: 全句是 the + 比较级, the + 比较级 结构：前一分句 The stronger the traffic...，后一分句 the more likely a person was to settle for the easier option，后者主干为 a person was likely to settle for the easier option。
sentenceNotes.structure: 两个分句都以 the 加比较级开头，表示“越……就越……”；between the two areas 是修饰 traffic 的介词短语；be likely to do 后接 settle for the easier option，settle for 意为“勉强接受、退而选择”。
sentenceNotes.translation: 两个脑区之间的信号传递越强，人就越容易退而选择较轻松的选项。
sentenceNotes.tip: 遇到 the more..., the more... 结构，先把两个分句各自还原成正常语序：traffic is stronger / a person was more likely to...。traffic 在这里不是“交通”，而是比喻信号往来。

sentenceNotes.sentence: The more depleted the brain feels, the steeper the price it puts on effort, so a reward that once looked attractive can suddenly seem not worth the trouble.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: 整体由 the more..., the steeper... 的比较结构与 so 引出的结果分句组成；结果分句主干为 a reward can seem not worth the trouble。
sentenceNotes.structure: 第一分句 The more depleted the brain feels 中 depleted 作表语；第二分句 the steeper the price it puts on effort 中 it puts on effort 是省略了关系词的定语从句，修饰 price；so 之后 a reward that once looked attractive 含 that 引导的定语从句，主句谓语为 can seem。
sentenceNotes.translation: 大脑越是感到被掏空，它给努力标出的价码就越高，于是原本看来诱人的回报，可能突然显得不值得费那个劲。
sentenceNotes.tip: 本句为编辑自拟练习句，并非原刊引文。抓住 put a price on 这一搭配（“给……定价”），再注意 so 前后是因果；not worth the trouble 是常见表达，意为“不值得费这个事”。
